Categories.value: Trams in Cape Town|Adderley Street, Cape Town|Cape Town in the 1890s|PD South-Africa|Template Unknown (author)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Historical images of Cape Town|Dennis Edwards, Publisher

ImageDescription.value: Original caption reads: "View of Adderley Street, Cape Town from Longmarket Street. This thoroughfare, which one might term "the leading street of South Africa", is thronged during the greater part of the day by a busy crowd of shoppers and pedestrians. The shops are for the most part situated on the north side of the street , and are decked with all the latest novelties from Europe. Electric trams start from the centre of Adderley Street for all parts of the town and suburbs, and are considered the finest and most complete "South of the line"."

ObjectName.value: Walter Sisulu Nasionale Botaniese Tuin, uitsig a

Categories.value: GFDL|Taken with Panasonic Lumix DMC-TZ8|Walter Sisulu National Botanical Garden|License migration redundant|Self-published work|Photographs by User:JMK

ImageDescription.value: Northeastward view over the Walter Sisulu National Botanical Garden in western Roodepoort, Gauteng, showing the vicinity of the reception area and the sprawling lawns flanking the footpaths. The footpath (leading diagonally over the scene) converges on Muldersdrift se Loop, the watercourse that bisects the gardens. Beyond the upper footbridge (out of view) this footpath arrives at the large lawn flanking the plunge pool of the waterfall over the Roodekrans. From the plunge pool, a visitor can take the Geological Trail, a very steep footpath to the top of the waterfall and the natural bankenveld vegetation beyond.
